findings.summary: In every desktop state capture, the front-page hero vignette appears as a bare saturated slab. The anchor card, chips, star and cloud are invisible or only ghosted, so the first screen reads as an unfinished block rather than the reference's composed scene (01, 02). The recipe animates every child of the vignette with fill-mode `both` and a staggered delay, but leaves the `::before` offset edge static. So whenever `is-in` is applied, the edge is the only thing showing until the build finishes.
findings.promptFix: A build animation must never make a finished illustration look broken at any frame. The vignette's offset edge (::before) builds with the anchor as one piece, first and with no delay; chips, star and cloud follow. A vignette already in view on first paint renders in its finished state with no build; `is-in` is only for vignettes that scroll into view. The whole build finishes within about one second.
findings.specRule: .ms-vignette::before { translate: var(--space-3) var(--space-3); background: var(--ms-edge, var(--color-field-orange)); } … .ms-vignette.is-in > * { animation: ms-build var(--motion-duration-vignette) var(--motion-easing-vignette) both; animation-delay: calc(var(--ms-i, 0) * var(--motion-duration-reveal)); }

findings.summary: On every night page, in all four apps, the footer ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer band. It is the only light surface on the page, while the reference's night palette stays dark to the edge (03). This has been open since rc.3. The spec maps the bar to `surface.inverse`, which is white at night.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in each appearance: ink by day, and a step darker than the navy page at night, with white text and icons in both. `surface.inverse` is only for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons

findings.summary: Stat-tile numbers are about 32px on desktop and 28px on phones, barely heavier than the bold label above them, so the tiles read as coloured cards rather than numbers. In the reference (08), one large bold figure, about twice that size, dominates each saturated field, with a small eyebrow above and the caption below. This was named in rc.4. The spec still sets the number at h3 and the label in bold.
findings.promptFix: In a stat tile the number is the tile. Set it at `font.size.h2` or larger, bold, with tight tracking. Set the label as a small eyebrow (`font.size.label`, medium, not bold) so only the figure is heavy. On phones keep the number at `font.size.h3` or larger, and shorten the caption rather than shrink the figure.
findings.specRule: Stat tile: … label `font.size.label` bold, number `font.size.h3` bold, caption `font.size.body`

findings.summary: In all three apps with a top bar, keyboard focus on top-bar links is still a square box drawn tight to the word, sometimes clipping the current-page dot. It looks like the browser default, where the reference draws a rounded ring offset around the whole control (11). Pills, switches and the menu circle get the right ring. This has been open since rc.2. The spec only says 'ring' for nav links, without a shape or offset.
findings.promptFix: Use one shared :focus-visible rule for every focusable element that is not a pill, input or card: a 2px `color.focus.ring` outline (ringOnField on saturated and night fields) with a 2px offset. It goes around the whole hit area, including a leading dot, with padding so the text never touches it. Corners are `radius.full` on nav links and `radius.sm` on inline links. Never a square box.

findings.summary: The dashboard's stat-tile plates fade in with a staggered reveal. In the captures, one plate is a ghost and the others are missing, so the shape kit is absent from the one saturated field on the screen. On data screens, decoration that arrives late reads as absent.
findings.promptFix: Reveal and stagger are for marketing sections only. On product screens (dashboards, lists, details, settings), plates, glyphs and stat-tile art render at once in their final state, like the data beside them.
findings.specRule: Confetti and plates fade in once (Reveal, staggered in reading order).

findings.summary: In light mode an off switch is a warm-grey track one tone away from the cream panel, so it nearly disappears beside the crisp ink on-switches. The reference's controls always hold a clear edge (09, 11). The night version is clear. This carries over from rc.4.
findings.promptFix: An off-switch track needs 3:1 contrast against the surface it sits on. On cream panels, use `color.border.strong` for the track, or a 2px `border.strong` ring around it, never a surface tone one step from the panel.

findings.summary: Some states are barely designed. Hovering a table row changes nothing visible. Newsletter success and a saved profile are a small tick and a word, and on desktop the saved tick sits below the first screen. The reference makes every state read at a glance and gives confirmations a designed moment (09, 11).

Some pictograms are below the reference's spot-pictogram craft (07). Blog cover pictograms fill only about a third of their cover, with the sparkle always in the same corner and only a thin offset edge for shading. Several settings plates (card, receipt, monitor) are flat front-on icons at half size. Every product page in the shop reuses one price-tag band cluster with the hues swapped, and the size tiles repeat one meaningless dot-in-ring glyph. The band scenes elsewhere are at the right standard.

Phone rhythm is coarser than the reference's (04) in three places. The arc of a header band lands directly on the next panel with no air. Small fact groups become stacked full-width cards, one value per slab. The shop catalogue becomes a run of full-width square colour slabs, one product per screen.

A lone blue confetti dot floats in the middle of the front-page hero below the pills on desktop and phone, attached to nothing. Marketing sections such as the about page open with plain left-hugging headings and no confetti. The reference places every small piece against a subject or in a deliberate scatter around a centred heading (02, 06).

Agent slips that are not in the spec: the open user menu is almost transparent; the confirmation sheet on phones renders at the end of the document; a colour tile's label touches its border; the checkout submit pill is cut off at the fold; the sidebar stops at the viewport height; a trend arrow hangs beside a wrapped caption.

notes: Review: 140/140 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/morning-shapes/0.1.0-rc.5/review-1).

At rest, rc.5 reads clearly as the reference's language in all four apps. It has the yolk and category-hue bands with arcs, ink pills on ledges, cream panels, saturated stat tiles and crescent-shaded flat pictograms, and a convincing derived night palette. The rc.4 gaps in band height, phone stacking and vignette composition have closed, and the family holds across the apps.

It stays below the reference's craft in these ways: (1) a spec-caused build animation leaves the hero as a bare slab in every desktop state capture; (2) the dark footer ends in a white bar; (3) stat figures are too small to dominate their tiles; (4) nav-link focus is square, off switches are faint, and hover and confirmation states are thin; (5) some pictograms are undersized or repeated. Items 1 to 3, the off switch and the focus ring have quotable fixes in the spec.
